title: How One Company Convinced the World Diamonds Are Rare
hook: In 2011, the most famous diamond company in the world was valued at almost thirteen billion dollars. This year, its owner is trying to sell most of it, for about one billion.
summary: In this video we follow De Beers from a shiny pebble on the Orange River in 1867 to Cecil Rhodes' takeover of Kimberley, the London warehouse that kept diamonds scarce, and the 1947 slogan "A Diamond Is Forever". Then we look at how new mines, a shrinking stockpile and lab-grown diamonds broke the spell, why diamond prices are falling, and what the sale of De Beers means for Botswana and for the ring on your finger. Update: in November 2026 Botswana named the Global Diamond Consortium, led by former De Beers boss Gareth Penny, as the winning bidder for Anglo American's stake; Botswana says it will become De Beers' largest shareholder.
